intro.headingLine1: A long way for a train,
paragraphs: Český Krumlov is the day trip visitors to Prague ask for most. The whole old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site: a castle with a painted tower above a tight bend of the Vltava, lanes of Renaissance houses below it, and one of the best-preserved Baroque theatres in Europe.

It is also about 2.5 hours from Prague. By train or coach that means a fixed timetable and a change on the way. By private car it is one seat from your hotel door to the edge of the old town, leaving when you choose and coming back when you have seen enough.
This page is about going there and back in one day. If you plan to stay overnight or continue to Vienna, Salzburg or Hallstatt, book a one-way transfer on the Prague to Český Krumlov route instead.

items.title: Leave early, arrive before the coaches
items.body: A start around 8:00 puts you in Český Krumlov by mid-morning, before the tour coaches fill the lanes. The return time is yours to set.

items.title: The castle and its tower
items.body: The State Castle is the second largest in the Czech Republic. The courtyards and gardens are free to walk; the tower, the interiors and the Baroque theatre need tickets, and theatre tours sell out in summer.

items.title: The old town on foot
items.body: The centre is closed to cars. Your chauffeur drops you at the car park by the old town, a few minutes’ walk from the main square, and waits there.

items.title: A stop on the way
items.body: The route passes České Budějovice and Hluboká Castle. Tell us when you book if you would like to stop at either and we confirm it in writing.

items.title: One price for the car
items.body: You pay for the car, not per person: the drive there and back, plus the time the chauffeur waits. The first 15 minutes of waiting are free; after that, waiting is charged for each started 15 minutes. The booking form shows the full total before you pay.

items.title: Child seats at no charge
items.body: Infant, toddler and booster seats are free. Tell us the children’s ages when you book and the right seats are fitted before pickup.

steps.label: How it works
steps.heading: Booking a day trip in four steps.

items.title: Send us the plan
items.body: Give the date, your Prague address, the town and how long you would like to stay — in the booking form or in a message. A rough outline of the day is enough.

items.title: Choose the car
items.body: E-Class for up to three, V-Class for up to six with room to spare, S-Class for an executive day. You see the full price for the car before you pay.

items.title: Meet your chauffeur
items.body: You receive the chauffeur’s name and phone number in advance. They collect you at your hotel or apartment door at the agreed time.

items.title: Take your time
items.body: The chauffeur waits near the centre for the time you booked. If you would like to stay longer on the day, tell the chauffeur: extra waiting is charged at the same rate.

editorial.label: Good to know
paragraphs: Wear shoes for cobbles: Český Krumlov is steep in places and entirely paved in stone. Castle interiors are closed on Mondays and in the winter months, though the courtyards, the old town and the views stay open all year.
Lunch is easy to find on the river terraces below the castle. In July and August reserve a table, or eat a little early.

Your chauffeur is a professional driver, not a tour guide: they know the road, where to drop you and where to wait, but they do not lead tours. Entrance tickets, meals and guided tours are not part of the price. If you would like a licensed local guide, book one for the hours you plan to be there and we time the drive around it.

faqs.q: How much is a private day trip from Prague to Český Krumlov?
faqs.a: The price depends on the car you choose and on how long you stay. It is made up of the drive there and back and the chauffeur’s waiting time: the first 15 minutes of waiting are free, and after that waiting is charged for each started 15 minutes. The price is for the whole car, with fuel and motorway tolls included, and you see the exact total in the booking form before you pay.

faqs.q: How long does the day trip take?
faqs.a: Plan about ten hours in total: roughly 2.5 hours each way and four to five hours in Český Krumlov. Leaving Prague at 8:00, you are back around 18:00. You choose both times.

faqs.q: Does the chauffeur wait and drive us back the same day?
faqs.a: Yes. The same car and chauffeur take you there, wait near the centre for the time you booked and drive you back to your Prague address. Waiting time is part of the price; if you decide to stay longer on the day, tell the chauffeur and the extra time is charged at the same rate.

faqs.q: Is a guide or entrance ticket included?
faqs.a: No. The price covers the car and the chauffeur. Tickets and guided tours are booked separately, and the chauffeur does not act as a guide. We are glad to time the day around a guide or a ticket slot you have booked.

faqs.q: Can we stop in České Budějovice or at Hluboká Castle?
faqs.a: Both are on the way. Tell us which stop you would like when you book, and we confirm the plan and the price in writing before the trip.

faqs.q: How many people fit in one car?
faqs.a: Up to three passengers in an E-Class or S-Class and up to six in a V-Class. Larger groups travel in two or more cars. Child seats are free in every class.
